o: the part a moving body holds because of its speed, least at the turning points
the rate at which the moving and stored parts of the motion trade places
the part a displaced body holds because of its position, greatest at the turning points
the continual exchange between moving and stored parts while their sum stays fixed
items.s: energy trade off: the continual exchange between moving and stored parts while their sum stays fixed. The other options describe kinetic contribution, stored contribution, power flow in a swing.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “behaviour in which the size of the restoring influence grows faster or slower than the displacement”
o: pendulum approximation
normal mode
non linear response
coupled oscillators
items.s: non linear response is behaviour in which the size of the restoring influence grows faster or slower than the displacement.

items.q: longitudinal wave may be defined as
o: a disturbance that transfers energy through space without transporting the material of the medium
the rate at which a crest advances through the medium
a travelling disturbance whose vibration lies along the direction of travel
a travelling disturbance whose crests are straight, parallel and equally spaced
items.s: longitudinal wave: a travelling disturbance whose vibration lies along the direction of travel. The other options describe wave, wave speed, plane wave.
items.t: Wave motion and the wave equation

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “driving an oscillator by changing one of its own properties rhythmically rather than by an outside push”
o: non linear response
chaotic motion
parametric excitation
anharmonic oscillator
items.s: parametric excitation is driving an oscillator by changing one of its own properties rhythmically rather than by an outside push.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spring constant?
o: the force needed per unit extension of an elastic coil
a hanging bob on a thread whose cycle time is exactly two units of a minute divided by thirty
the resting place of an oscillator where no restoring pull acts
a block attached to an elastic coil that oscillates when displaced from rest
items.s: spring constant: the force needed per unit extension of an elastic coil. The other options describe equilibrium position, mass spring system, seconds pendulum.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains natural frequency.
o: the motion of an oscillator driven by a repeated external push
the progressive loss of amplitude of an oscillation because energy is steadily removed
the constant that fixes the rate at which the amplitude of a decaying oscillation shrinks
the rate at which a system oscillates freely when left to itself
items.s: natural frequency: the rate at which a system oscillates freely when left to itself. The other options describe damping coefficient, forced oscillation, damping.

items.q: “a moving emitter whose waves are crowded so the observed rate rises” is the definition of
o: receding source
Doppler effect
approaching source
observer in motion
items.s: approaching source is a moving emitter whose waves are crowded so the observed rate rises.

items.q: The correct meaning of turning point is
o: the constant total of moving and stored parts that a freely running oscillation keeps
the energy transferred when an elastic coil is stretched or compressed through a distance
the position at which a swung body momentarily comes to rest and reverses
the continual exchange between moving and stored parts while their sum stays fixed
items.s: turning point: the position at which a swung body momentarily comes to rest and reverses. The other options describe energy trade off, energy budget of a swing, work done by a spring.

items.q: In this course, equilibrium position refers to
o: a small heavy bob hanging on a light thread from a fixed point
a body hung from a wire that twists and untwists about its own axis
a hanging bob on a thread whose cycle time is exactly two units of a minute divided by thirty
the resting place of an oscillator where no restoring pull acts
items.s: equilibrium position: the resting place of an oscillator where no restoring pull acts. The other options describe simple pendulum, seconds pendulum, torsional oscillator.

items.q: The correct meaning of end correction is
o: a tube stopped at one end, supporting only odd multiples of the lowest frequency
a region of a sound wave where the particles are spread apart
a measure of loudness stated on a logarithmic scale in decibel
the small extra length added to a pipe to allow for the disturbance spreading beyond its open end
items.s: end correction: the small extra length added to a pipe to allow for the disturbance spreading beyond its open end. The other options describe rarefaction, closed pipe, sound level.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines wave speed?
o: how many complete cycles are contained in a unit of length
the distance between two successive points in step on a wave
the rate at which a crest advances through the medium
a surface joining all points of a wave that are in the same phase
items.s: wave speed: the rate at which a crest advances through the medium. The other options describe wave number, wavefront, wavelength.
items.t: Wave motion and the wave equation

items.q: “the distance between two successive points in step on a wave” is the definition of
o: transverse wave
wave
wavelength
wave speed
items.s: wavelength is the distance between two successive points in step on a wave.
items.t: Wave motion and the wave equation

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a region of a sound wave where the particles are crowded together”
o: compression
open pipe
closed pipe
resonance tube
items.s: compression is a region of a sound wave where the particles are crowded together.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains fundamental.
o: the portion of a standing pattern between two neighbouring fixed points
a point on a standing wave that never moves
the lowest frequency at which a system can stand in a stable pattern
the rule that at any point the resultant displacement is the sum of the displacements of the separate waves
items.s: fundamental: the lowest frequency at which a system can stand in a stable pattern. The other options describe loop, node, superposition principle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines observer in motion?
o: a listener whose own movement changes the rate at which waves reach the ear
the piled up disturbance formed when an emitter outruns the waves it produces
the shock disturbance produced when a source travels faster than the waves it emits
the lengthening of observed wavelength from a source moving away
items.s: observer in motion: a listener whose own movement changes the rate at which waves reach the ear. The other options describe shock wavefront, red shift, sonic boom.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains period.
o: twice pi times the number of cycles per second
the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation
the distance of an oscillator from its central position at a given instant
the stage a cycle has reached at a given instant, stated as an angle
items.s: period: the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation. The other options describe angular frequency, phase, displacement.

items.q: “a travelling disturbance whose crests are straight, parallel and equally spaced” is the definition of
o: transverse wave
plane wave
wave
wave speed
items.s: plane wave is a travelling disturbance whose crests are straight, parallel and equally spaced.
items.t: Wave motion and the wave equation

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains wavefront.
o: how many complete cycles are contained in a unit of length
a travelling disturbance whose crests are straight, parallel and equally spaced
a disturbance that transfers energy through space without transporting the material of the medium
a surface joining all points of a wave that are in the same phase
items.s: wavefront: a surface joining all points of a wave that are in the same phase. The other options describe wave, wave number, plane wave.
items.t: Wave motion and the wave equation

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation”
o: phase
restoring influence
angular frequency
period
items.s: period is the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains restoring influence.
o: the distance of an oscillator from its central position at a given instant
the pull or push that always acts to bring an oscillator back towards its central position
twice pi times the number of cycles per second
the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation
items.s: restoring influence: the pull or push that always acts to bring an oscillator back towards its central position. The other options describe displacement, angular frequency, period.

items.q: The correct meaning of antinode is
o: a point on a standing wave that never moves
the rule that at any point the resultant displacement is the sum of the displacements of the separate waves
a point on a standing wave that swings with the greatest amplitude
a frequency above the lowest at which a system can stand in a stable pattern
items.s: antinode: a point on a standing wave that swings with the greatest amplitude. The other options describe overtone, node, superposition principle.

items.q: “a fixed pattern of still points and swinging points produced by two equal trains travelling in opposite directions” is the definition of
o: standing wave
node
fundamental
harmonic
items.s: standing wave is a fixed pattern of still points and swinging points produced by two equal trains travelling in opposite directions.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the distance of an oscillator from its central position at a given instant”
o: angular frequency
displacement
restoring influence
simple harmonic motion
items.s: displacement is the distance of an oscillator from its central position at a given instant.

items.q: The correct meaning of interference pattern is
o: the arrangement of reinforcement and cancellation produced where two waves overlap
the fraction of a cycle by which one wave leads or lags another
the condition of two waves whose crests arrive at the same instant
the slow rise and fall of loudness heard when two nearly equal frequencies sound together
items.s: interference pattern: the arrangement of reinforcement and cancellation produced where two waves overlap. The other options describe phase difference, beats, in phase.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines amplitude?
o: the greatest displacement of an oscillator from its central position
twice pi times the number of cycles per second
the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation
the stage a cycle has reached at a given instant, stated as an angle
items.s: amplitude: the greatest displacement of an oscillator from its central position. The other options describe phase, period, angular frequency.

items.q: In this course, restoring influence refers to
o: twice pi times the number of cycles per second
the distance of an oscillator from its central position at a given instant
the pull or push that always acts to bring an oscillator back towards its central position
the stage a cycle has reached at a given instant, stated as an angle
items.s: restoring influence: the pull or push that always acts to bring an oscillator back towards its central position. The other options describe displacement, angular frequency, phase.

items.q: In this course, large amplitude effect refers to
o: the small swing simplification that treats the restoring influence of a hanging bob as proportional to its displacement
the lengthening of the period of a hanging oscillator that occurs as its swing grows
driving an oscillator by changing one of its own properties rhythmically rather than by an outside push
a vibrating body whose restoring influence is not proportional to the displacement
items.s: large amplitude effect: the lengthening of the period of a hanging oscillator that occurs as its swing grows. The other options describe anharmonic oscillator, parametric excitation, pendulum approximation.

items.q: The correct meaning of closed pipe is
o: the small extra length added to a pipe to allow for the disturbance spreading beyond its open end
a measure of loudness stated on a logarithmic scale in decibel
a tube stopped at one end, supporting only odd multiples of the lowest frequency
a pipe used with a tuning source to find the lengths that give the loudest response
items.s: closed pipe: a tube stopped at one end, supporting only odd multiples of the lowest frequency. The other options describe sound level, resonance tube, end correction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines wave?
o: the rate at which a crest advances through the medium
a travelling disturbance whose vibration is at right angles to the direction of travel
a disturbance that transfers energy through space without transporting the material of the medium
a travelling disturbance whose vibration lies along the direction of travel
items.s: wave: a disturbance that transfers energy through space without transporting the material of the medium. The other options describe transverse wave, longitudinal wave, wave speed.
